about: The written pieces scripts/ly-to-mei.js converts from Mutopia Project LilyPond files (docs/reference/findings/2026-11-20-public-domain-scores.md, findings 16 and 20; downloaded with the operator's permission on 2026-11-20). Per piece: the files and their SHA-256 (checked before converting), the main file, the words for the MEI header, each staff's label (and a transposition the source leaves to the player), and tempo words the source writes without a number, with the number the piece plays them at.

fur_elise.title: Für Elise (Clavierstück in A minor, WoO 59)
fur_elise.availability: Public domain. Beethoven's Für Elise, WoO 59, as Breitkopf & Härtel printed it in 1888 (Ludwig van Beethovens Werke, Serie 25, No. 298). Converted to MEI by HumanityOS (scripts/ly-to-mei.js, 2026-11-20) from Mutopia Project piece 931, typeset in LilyPond by Stelios Samelis and placed in the public domain by the typesetter (Mutopia-2015/08/18-931). The conversion is dedicated to the public domain (CC0).
comment: Für Elise, WoO 59, by Ludwig van Beethoven: written music for HumanityOS's score player (docs/design/score-player.md).
Edition: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1888. Licence: public domain (docs/reference/findings/2026-11-20-public-domain-scores.md, finding 20).
Converted by scripts/ly-to-mei.js. The pedal line is left out; the hidden metronome mark of the LilyPond file (a quarter note at 72) is kept as the tempo.
Open it in MuseScore 4.2 or later, or any text editor; change a note and the game plays the change the next time the piece starts.

mountain_king.title: In the Hall of the Mountain King (Peer Gynt Suite No. 1, Op. 46, No. 4)
mountain_king.availability: Public domain. Grieg's own piano arrangement of In the Hall of the Mountain King, Op. 46 No. 4, as The University Society printed it in 1918 (IMSLP #00581). Converted to MEI by HumanityOS (scripts/ly-to-mei.js, 2026-11-20) from Mutopia Project piece 1888, typeset in LilyPond by Coyau and placed in the public domain by the typesetter (Mutopia-2013/12/07-1888). The conversion is dedicated to the public domain (CC0).
comment: In the Hall of the Mountain King, Op. 46 No. 4, by Edvard Grieg, in Grieg's own piano arrangement: written music for HumanityOS's score player (docs/design/score-player.md).
Edition: The University Society, New York, 1918. Licence: public domain (docs/reference/findings/2026-11-20-public-domain-scores.md, finding 16).

Converted by scripts/ly-to-mei.js. The right hand's two voices (LilyPond's part-combined rightOne and rightTwo) are layers 1 and 2 of staff 1; the pedal marks are left out; the closing tremolos are written out as sixteenth notes.
Open it in MuseScore 4.2 or later, or any text editor; change a note and the game plays the change the next time the piece starts.

beethoven_symphony5_1.title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67: I. Allegro con brio
beethoven_symphony5_1.availability: Public domain. The first movement of Beethoven's Symphony No. 5, Op. 67, as Breitkopf & Härtel printed it in 1862 to 1865 (Ludwig van Beethovens Werke, Serie 1, No. 5). Converted to MEI by HumanityOS (scripts/ly-to-mei.js, 2026-11-20) from Mutopia Project piece 941, typeset in LilyPond by Stelios Samelis, adapted to LilyPond 2.16.2 by Johannes Heinecke, and placed in the public domain by the typesetter (Mutopia-2017/11/05-941). The conversion is dedicated to the public domain (CC0).
comment: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67, first movement, by Ludwig van Beethoven: written music for HumanityOS's score player (docs/design/score-player.md).

Source: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=941 (Symphony5_1-lys.zip, SHA-256 a0165591776ac4f277ff4331b075774d739639726f26f162aad57761554abf80; each file's own SHA-256 is in scripts/ly-to-mei.pieces.json).
Edition: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1862-1865. Licence: public domain (docs/reference/findings/2026-11-20-public-domain-scores.md, finding 20).

Converted by scripts/ly-to-mei.js. Tempo numbers are not printed in this edition: Allegro con brio plays at a half note = 108 (216 quarter notes a minute, Beethoven's own metronome mark of 1817), the oboe's Adagio cadenza at 60 quarter notes a minute and the Allegro again after it; these are playback values (midi.bpm), the words are the edition's.

The double basses sound an octave below the written notes (trans.semi -12), as the instrument does; the clarinets in B flat and the horns in E flat are written as they read them (trans.semi -2 and -9).
Open it in MuseScore 4.2 or later, or any text editor; change a note and the game plays the change the next time the piece starts.
